nodes.label: The Selfless Caregiver
nodes.description: Carrying the entire burden of caretaking alone while suppressing personal needs.
summary: Expected Daniel to understand and share the caretaking load without explicitly asking previously.
Felt deep shame after yelling at her mother because she believes she should always be a calm caregiver.

quotes.text: Nobody asked me what I wanted! You decided and I went along with it because that's what I do!

nodes.label: Inherited Coping Patterns
nodes.description: Unconsciously repeating family histories of alcohol use to numb painful emotions.
summary: Finished an entire bottle of wine after the argument with Daniel and her mother.
Noticed she sits in the exact same chair and does the same thing her father used to do.

quotes.text: And now I'm sitting in the same kitchen he sat in, doing the same thing.

nodes.label: The Invisible Anger
nodes.description: Holding in months of resentment until it erupts into explosive outbursts.
summary: Described the outburst as months of pressure finding the smallest crack.
Felt torn between apologizing for yelling and standing by the truth of her anger.

quotes.text: It came out of nowhere, but it didn't come out of nowhere at all.

nodes.label: Apologizing Takes Everything Back
nodes.description: Assuming that expressing regret invalidates the truth of one's feelings.
summary: Expressed fear that apologizing to Daniel meant giving up her valid need for help.

quotes.text: In my family if you apologize, you take everything back.

nodes.label: My Outbursts Make Me Bad
nodes.description: Equating a momentary loss of emotional control with being a terrible person.
summary: Blamed herself entirely for the argument because she yelled in front of her mother.

quotes.text: I felt awful. Physically, and just... ashamed. Because the whole thing was my fault.

nodes.label: Numbing With Wine
nodes.description: Using alcohol as an evening reward and mechanism to put things down.
summary: Drank a whole bottle of wine alone in the kitchen after the family left.
Noticed herself anticipating the glass of wine starting as early as 3 p.m.

quotes.text: Like at 3 p.m. I'll think, 'Just get through till tonight, and then you can have your glass.'

nodes.label: Passive Acquiescence
nodes.description: Going along with decisions made by others without voicing personal desires.
summary: Recognized that she often goes along with decisions rather than voicing her own needs.

quotes.text: You decided and I went along with it because that's what I do!

nodes.label: Walking Before Wine
nodes.description: Introducing a gentle physical pause before resorting to alcohol use.
summary: Agreed to try taking a walk around the block after her mother is in bed before opening wine.

quotes.text: Maybe... I could go for a walk after Mom's in bed. Not a run... But a walk around the block.

nodes.label: Recognition and Being Seen
nodes.description: Longing to have one's hard work and emotional reality acknowledged by others.
summary: Expressed a deep desire for her brother to acknowledge how hard caretaking is for her.
Connected her emotional pain directly to the lack of being seen by her partner.

quotes.text: I want him to say, 'This is hard, and I see that you're doing most of it.'

nodes.label: Rest and Restoration
nodes.description: Needing physical and mental breaks from relentless caregiving duties.
summary: Proposed a respite program to secure one weekend a month away from caretaking.
Reflected on past creative hobbies like pottery where her hands were busy and brain stopped.

quotes.text: Like a weekend a month where Mom stays somewhere with care so I can have a break.

nodes.label: Connection and Partnership
nodes.description: Longing for genuine companionship and shared support with her sibling.
summary: Expressed deep loneliness and a desire to reconnect with her brother as a sibling.

quotes.text: Where we can just be... siblings.

nodes.label: Family Loyalty
nodes.description: Deep commitment to caring for aging parents and maintaining family bonds.
summary: Dedicates her time and energy to caring for her mother daily despite the immense toll.

quotes.text: He's the only other person who knows what this is like — he's her son.

nodes.label: Authenticity and Honesty
nodes.description: Valuing emotional truth and clear communication over keeping the peace.
summary: Realized that separating her apology from her truth felt clean and honest.

quotes.text: Scary. But clean, somehow. Like it's the actual truth.

edges.explanation: Her need to be seen by Daniel clashes with her narrative of silently carrying everything alone.
Using wine to cope directly feeds into her painful narrative of repeating her father's drinking habits.
Her hidden anger builds up precisely because she lives by the selfless caregiver narrative.
Believing she cannot apologize without taking everything back reinforces her pattern of self-silencing.
Her intense shame stems from failing her own impossible standard as a selfless caregiver.
Quietly going along with decisions is the behavioral manifestation of her caregiver narrative.
Taking a walk before drinking is a new strategy designed to interrupt her inherited drinking pattern.
Wanting rest and respite directly challenges her narrative of enduring all caretaking tasks alone.
Her loneliness and desire for partnership highlight the isolated reality of her caregiving role.
Her deep commitment to family loyalty compels her to remain in the selfless caregiver role.
Valuing authenticity helps her find a way to honor her anger rather than keeping it hidden.
